title: Solo Sentry — quick run & handoff sketch
content:
Context: I picked up a short solo weekend stretch. This is a terse brain-dump of what I did, what I saw, and fragile shortcuts to keep the stack healthy until a fuller runbook is merged (see linked confluence).

Summary (first 1hr):
- Checked alerts dashboard: /console/alerts -> filtered by severity=P1,P2. Note: spike in tokenization errors last night (look at model-q1 pods).
- Pager activity: none since 02:10. Slack #oncall had a brief thread re: HTTP 503s for /v1/generate — likely transient LB config.

Quick triage checklist (solo-friendly):
1) Confirm incident: `curl -sS -I https://api.redwood.test/health` -> expect 200/OK. If 500+, open channel #oncall and post status.
2) Inspect recent deploys: `gh pr list --label=deploy --state=merged --json number,title` (or check /deployments page). If deploy within 30m -> suspect rollout.
3) Check pods: `kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep model-q1` then `kubectl logs -f <pod> -c runtime` for errors containing "kvcache" or "oom-kill".
4) If low memory OOMs: scale down batch_size via feature-flag in /console/route-config, or restart the pod with previous revision. Fast command to restart: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-q1-deploy -n inference`
5) If 503s at LB level: look at envoy logs on edge nodes: `ssh ops-edge-1 journalctl -u envoy -n 200` (edge cred in 1Password).

Temporary mitigation patterns I used: 
- Toggle auto-batching -> reduced CPU by ~15% (temp). Path: Console -> Routes -> /v1/generate -> batching -> target=low.
- Revert recent PR (infra PR #889) if rollout correlates with error spike. Revert steps in the PR description.

Notes for next oncall (handoff):
- Watch for tokenization-errors: logs show "tokenize: invalid byte sequence" — likely model tokenizer mismatch after a model swap. If this persists, pin route to model-q1:v3 instead of v4.
- Model cache growth: KV cache size reached 92% on one host; set `KV_CACHE_MAX=60%` in experiment page in Console to prevent host-wide oom.

Open questions / TODOs (follow up after shift):
- Add 1-click circuit-breaker to Console to quickly disable batching across routes. Filed CON-71 on Confluence.
- Improve alert thresholds for tokenization errors (current alert floods Slack).
- Write a short automated script to collect: envoy logs + model pod logs + recent deploys into a zipped artifact for postmortem.

Snippets and bookmarks:
- Health check: https://api.redwood.test/health
- Dashboards: https://console.redwood.internal/dash/alerts, https://console.redwood.internal/dash/latency
- Oncall Slack: https://workspace.slack.com/archives/ONCALL
- Confluence runbook (draft): https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/ON/primary-runbook

Rapid commands cheat-sheet:
- kubectl get pods -n inference | grep model-q1
- kubectl logs -n inference <pod> -c runtime --tail=200
- kubectl rollout undo deploy/model-q1-deploy -n inference --to-revision=3
- gh pr view 889 --repo redwood-inference/infra --json body

Personal observations:
- System feels more sensitive after the autoscaler changes last cycle; be conservative with aggressive scaling policies during weekends.
- If you need to make a change, announce it in #oncall and add a small rollback note in the PR title so the next person can see it quickly.

End-of-shift checklist (what I did):
- Left a note in #oncall summarizing actions taken and why (link to this doc).
- Opened JIRA-ONC-412 to track recurring tokenization errors.
- Reverted staging infra PR (889) and monitored for 40m; error rate dropped to baseline.

If anything is unclear ping me directly (Slack DMs) — Aisha.

-- scratch notes:
- saw intermittent 429s around 03:12 UTC tied to burst-throttle. Temporary fix: increase `burst_window` for dedicated pool group to 200ms.
- log grep: `grep -R "kvcache" /var/log/modelq1/* | tail -n 50`
